description: Varifocal Loss on predicted probabilities and continuous IoU-aware scores, with q-weighted positive binary cross-entropy and alpha*p^gamma-weighted negative binary cross-entropy (VarifocalNet paper §4.2 Eq. (2), .autopilot/sources/paper.txt:189-206). avg_factor supports N_pos normalization from §4.6 Eq. (3), .autopilot/sources/paper.txt:251-271, following the mean-reduction pattern in src/topologies/implementations/losses/quality_focal_loss.py:74-80; Trainer forwards loss_kwargs in src/topologies/training/losses.py:196-200.

examples.code:
import tempfile
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from topologies import Trainer, build, synth
root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
@synth.generator
def samples(ctx):
    features = torch.randn(4, generator=ctx.rng.torch)
    targets = torch.rand(2, generator=ctx.rng.torch)
    return {"inputs": synth.Tensor(features), "targets": synth.Tensor(targets)}
ds = synth.Spec("varifocal-iacs", generator=samples, size=8, splits={"train": 1.0}, seed=7, root=root, monitor="none").run()
train = ds.for_recipe("regression", split="train", input_field="inputs", target_field="targets", preserve_shape=True)
model = nn.Sequential(build("mlp", "tiny", in_features=4, out_features=2), nn.Sigmoid())
trainer = Trainer(model, train, recipe="regression", recipe_config={"loss": "varifocal-loss", "loss_kwargs": {"alpha": 0.75, "gamma": 2.0}}, batch_size=4, max_epochs=1, device="cpu")
trainer.fit()
examples.title: Train an IoU-aware classifier with Varifocal Loss

name: Varifocal Loss

parameters.additional parameters: alpha, gamma, and avg_factor only; unrecognized keyword parameters raise ValueError
parameters.alpha: finite nonnegative negative-example balancing factor (default 0.75; VarifocalNet paper §5.1.1)
parameters.avg_factor: optional finite positive denominator for the summed loss; accepted only with mean reduction (default None), pass N_pos for paper §4.6 Eq. (3)
parameters.gamma: finite nonnegative negative-example focusing exponent (default 2.0; VarifocalNet paper §5.1.1)
parameters.ignore_index: must be None because continuous quality targets have no ignored-index convention
parameters.logits_or_prediction: nonempty finite floating-point predicted probabilities in [0, 1], with any shape
parameters.reduction: none returns elementwise losses, mean averages all elements, or sum totals them (default mean)
parameters.targets: finite floating-point continuous quality targets in [0, 1], with the same shape and device as predictions
